records.observation: Extends java.awt.Color implements Comparable/DataIO. BYTESIZE5: write packed getRGB int then modifiable boolean. DataInput constructor reads packed int with hasAlpha=true then boolean; readObject(DataInput) only logs should NOT called and consumes nothing, so generic DataIO read usage would not deserialize. Default constructor opaque pink255/192/203, RGB ctor alpha255, Color copy preservesRGBA, Color+alpha replaces alpha; these set modifiabletrue, explicit RGBA/bool accepts flag, no flag accessors/setters here. Flag does not itself enforce mutation policy in this class. Typed equals(ColorAlpha) compares RGB only (ignores alpha/flag), no equals(Object) override shown, so overload differs from inherited dispatch. compareTo casts ColorAlpha; if RGB equal0 else other lengthSq minus own, thus descending R²+G²+B² with different same-norm RGB also0. Null/wrong type unguarded; channel square sums bounded for ordinary Color. Default palette creates216 triples from0,51,102,153,204,255 and sorts array, retains all despite comparison ties; sets global next index1. getNext uses index%(length-1)=mod215, increments signed int, returns shared palette entry: visits1..214,0 repeatedly, excludes index215 (black minimum norm), includes white index0 on wrap. Counter overflow eventually gives negative remainder/index; no synchronization or per-name mapping. ColorNameMap fallback calls this each unknown lookup, so same unknown name can receive successive colors. Static white191,white255,yellow255 instances modifiabletrue.
